paragraphs: He is mentioned in the Tosefta, at the end of Bava Kamma, as having been a launderer, and he was a great pious man. Hyman says this is not Abba Oshaya of Tireh, who was an Amora.[^1][^2]

notes.text: סוף ב״ק is end of Tosefta Bava Kamma, not the unverified model chapter 11 suggestion. טיראה/טריא are different place spellings rendered Tira/Tireh, without a modern location identity. Machine מיראה differs from supplied טיראה.

ואין זה is Hyman’s explicit nonidentity assertion, preserved with its force rather than an independent admission. Launderer and great pious man apply to Yeshayah, Amora to Abba Oshaya. None supplies an absent Rabbi title; Abba is explicit.
